entities.name: Bernat de Puigcercós
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bernat de Puigcercós (O.P.), a formidable Catalan Dominican friar, emerged as a pivotal figure in the ecclesiastical landscape of the 14th century, serving as the General Inquisitor for the Crown of Aragon. His tenure, culminating in his death in 1342, coincided with a period of intense religious scrutiny and the institutional consolidation of the Inquisition across Iberia. Puigcercós was not merely an administrator but a driving force in defining and enforcing orthodox doctrine, directly influencing the spiritual and intellectual climate of territories spanning Catalonia, Aragon, Valencia, and the Balearic Islands.

During his active years, Puigcercós presided over numerous inquisitorial processes, particularly targeting suspected heresy, Jewish converts (Conversos), and even members of other religious orders deemed heterodox. He played a crucial role in the prosecution of spiritual movements and individuals whose interpretations challenged established Church authority, thereby contributing to the suppression of intellectual dissent. His extensive jurisdiction meant that his decisions had far-reaching implications for individuals and communities, often resulting in severe penalties, including public penance, confiscation of property, and sometimes execution.

Puigcercós's legacy is intrinsically linked to the strengthening of the Holy Office within the Crown of Aragon, embedding its procedures and authority more deeply into the fabric of medieval Aragonese society. He helped establish precedents and institutional mechanisms that would endure for centuries, influencing the later, more centralized Spanish Inquisition. His actions contributed to a climate of religious conformity and solidified the Dominican Order's preeminent role in theological policing, leaving an indelible mark on the religious and legal history of the Iberian Peninsula.

His actions directly contributed to the suppression of diverse religious expressions and solidified the Dominican Order's authority in medieval Iberian society.
